- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast peak by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates momentum; add 2–5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast horizon) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% upward bias to early forecast points to compensate for lag.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to fully capitalize; increase forecast slope or peak by 3–5% to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history: if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion, suppress model’s tendency to follow recent highs; apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to avoid over-optimism.
